questions.question: When a transit vehicle signals to get back on the main road after stopping, what must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any transit vehicle signaling to return to the main road after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: T intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming. Be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the pavement. Keep both hands on the wheel and turn slightly into the right lane. Check for traffic before steering back on.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you and them.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors constantly to spot tailgaters early. If someone is following too closely, slow down gradually and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink if you will drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert others.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without emergency braking. This prevents the driver behind you from hitting your vehicle.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Gradually slow down while checking the rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check mirrors as you slow down. Move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when the path is clear.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces clear vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and lowers your inhibitions, making you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Warns about road conditions or hazards ahead.
Directs you to cities and towns.
Tells you traffic laws and rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns about road conditions or hazards ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to road conditions or hazards ahead. They are diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving. Being awake 18 hours impairs driving like a 0.05% blood alcohol level. Being awake 24 hours straight impairs driving like a 0.10% blood alcohol level.

questions.question: You have an upsetting incident at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are angry or upset, you should calm down before driving. Driving while angry is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver space to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver space to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver wants to pass you, slow down. This gives them enough room to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires ride on water instead of gripping the road. Low tire pressure, worn tire tread, and speeding on wet roads all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, when exiting a highway, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only proceed when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When a car approaches you with bright headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your high beams until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car has high beams on, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the lights.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: A reduced speed zone is starting.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: The "End school zone" sign marks the end of a reduced speed school zone. You must follow the school zone speed limit during the times posted.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your car.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Get a ride home with a sober friend.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a sober friend.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid driving while impaired is to arrange a ride with a friend who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol's effects. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: When passing on a multi-lane highway, you should:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, then go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off before crossing.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips to stay alert. Stop often to rest and stretch your body, even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see railroad tracks ahead, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop. A train or other vehicle may be using the tracks.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as:
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic signal has the same meaning as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe. A stop sign may be posted at this location as well.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it on a regulatory sign mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drivers must drive below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and red and black markings. A red circle with a slash over a symbol means that action is forbidden.
